verdicts.why: The brief does not decide tiling seams, and the 32 px/cell play-zoom copy was not given (subject.json says how many cells one repeat spans is not measured). Seen: terrain.png has a 1 px darker frame on all four edges. The outermost row and column average 84-87 luma; the next row and column in average 92-95. 99% of edge pixels are darker than their inner neighbour. Edge-to-edge wrap difference is 4.9 levels, against 2.7-2.9 between interior neighbours. In tiled_2x2.png this shows as a thin dark grid line, horizontal and vertical, at every join. That would draw a grid across polluted slime ground on the map. The sibling (sibling_unpolluted.png) has no such frame: its edge dip is about 2 levels and inconsistent (70%). No lettered line (A1-F1) names seams or edge frames, so this cannot be a REDO under the brief. Everything else passes: the candidate is our own drawing, not the donor (donor_standin.png is near-black grey with red-haloed spots; the candidate is olive moss with grey pocked patches). It has no outline, is a full 1024x1024 RGB canvas with no backdrop or prop, and there is no owner keep and no owner note. Concern for the owner: the candidate reads as olive moss or lichen camouflage, not as a polluted version of the bright lime, bubbled gel in sibling_unpolluted.png. The patch edges are scalloped blobs, which may be procedural. I could not prove it is script-drawn, and the placeholder_detect.py result was not given. The unpolluted sibling has no keep, so B3 does not bind.

proposals: Terrain tiling: a terrain texture must wrap with no visible seam. Its edge rows and columns carry no frame, keyline or value step; the wrap-around difference should stay near the interior neighbour difference; and the tiled 2x2 shows no line at the joins. Evidence: terrain.png edge rows and columns are about 8-10 luma darker than the next row or column in (99% of edge pixels), and tiled_2x2.png shows a dark grid at every join. Smallest fix: drop the outer 1 px and wrap-pad (or regenerate with circular padding), then re-tile to check.

Polluted-variant identity: a pollutedTexturePath should read as the same material as its unpolluted texturePath, with pollution added (darkened, stained, tinted), not as a different ground. Evidence: sibling_unpolluted.png is bright lime gel with bubble craters and membrane ridges; terrain.png is olive and brown moss-like blotches with grey pocked patches. Applies only once the owner keeps the unpolluted sibling or rules on it.
Terrain inputs: for terrain subjects the window should measure the repeat span (cells per file repeat) and supply a play-zoom render at that span, so B2 and D1 can be judged rather than skipped.

For a TerrainDef, define the play-zoom input: tile the file at a measured or assumed cells-per-repeat and downsample it to 32 px/cell, or state that a terrain needs no play-zoom copy. Until then every terrain judgment ends UNSURE however good the art is (subject.json; terrain.png).

Add a tiling-seam line for terrain: after a 2x2 tile, no visible line or step at the joins. The wrap step should be within about 1.5x the interior neighbour step (donor textures measure 1.0-1.2x). No lettered line covers this now, and before_repair.png shipped with a 1 px dark frame that drew a grid across the map (tiled_2x2.png now shows the fix).

Polluted terrain variants: a line requiring that a polluted variant read as the same ground as its unpolluted sibling, with pollution added, even when the sibling has no keep. terrain.png reads as olive moss, while sibling_unpolluted.png is bright lime bubbled gel. B3 binds only on keeps.
Give the judge the placeholder_detect.py result for every candidate, so E2 is measured and not only judged by eye. The scalloped patch edges in terrain.png could be procedural.

window_verdict.basis: Both looks found no lettered line (A1-F1) broken; no REDO and no refusal record. The first look's UNSUREs named one point no line covers: a 1-px dark frame and a weak wrap step, a grid line at every repeat in game (measured: frame 3-26 levels, wrap up to 6x; donors 0-2 and 1.0-1.2x). The second look checked repair v1 and found it drew the old wrap seam at the midline of each border band (UNSURE on 3; measured on all 15). Repair v3 removes the frame and cross-fades the wrap without a shifted copy: measured frame <= 0.8, wrap 0.97-1.23x, worst straight line in the file and across the wrap <= 1.52x the median step (donors 1.5-8.7x), and a 2x2 tile shows no line by eye. The brief allows no third look (§When the look is enough, and when to stop), so v3 stands on its measurements. A Slime UNSURE on the second look was for the missing play-zoom input, which the brief does not define for a terrain (proposal).
